Match each word-bank tile to the correct numbered target slot
Tip: use the word bank like draggable labels. Click any tile to spotlight that structure, then mentally place it in the correct numbered slot.
Study the flower, then match the terms

text.tspan: 1. Follow the arrows from each numbered slot
to a structure on the flower.
2. Choose a label from the word bank.
3. Use Hint or Check Answer whenever
This is a static SVG mock lesson.

g.text: down the style to the ovary.
Click a tile to spotlight a structure, then match it to the correct slot
Petals are often colorful and scented. They attract pollinators such as insects and birds.
Sepals are usually green outer structures that protect the flower when it is still in bud.
The pistil is the flower’s main female structure. It includes the stigma, style, and ovary.
The stigma is the sticky tip of the pistil. It catches pollen during pollination.
The style is the narrow stalk connecting the stigma at the top to the ovary below.
Anthers sit at the tips of stamens and produce pollen grains.
A filament is the slender stalk of a stamen. It supports the anther.
A stamen is the flower’s male structure. It is made of an anther and a filament.
The ovary holds ovules. After fertilization, it can develop into a fruit.
The receptacle is the thickened base where the flower’s parts attach.
Use these clues to narrow down each label before checking the full answer key.
They are often brightly colored and help attract pollinators.
Answer: think of the blossom’s colorful display.
These sit below the petals and protect the flower bud.
They are usually green rather than pink or yellow.
Anther + filament together make one complete male part.
If you know the pieces, you can name the whole structure.
Stigma + style + ovary together form the pistil.
The top catches pollen, the tube connects, and the base holds ovules.
The stigma is the sticky part that receives pollen.
The ovary is swollen and rounded.
The receptacle is the base where all parts attach.
How to reason through the board
Start with the easiest visible clues:
• The pink showy parts are petals.
• The green outer parts are sepals.
• The yellow pollen sacs are anthers.
• The thin stalk beneath an anther is a filament.
• The pistil runs through the center: stigma at the top, style as the tube, ovary at the base.
• The receptacle is the flower’s base where the upper parts connect.
Here is the complete answer key for the numbered target slots.
The rounded swollen base is the ovary.
The green platform under it is the receptacle.
Quick recap: slot order = petal, sepal, pistil, stigma, style, anther, filament, stamen, ovary, receptacle.
